horayot-10a-18-20.note: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua were traveling by ship. The voyage ran long, Rabban Gamliel's bread ran out, and he lived on the flour Rabbi Yehoshua had brought, explaining that a star rising once in seventy years misleads sailors. Amazed that so wise a man had to sail for a living, Rabban Gamliel heard of two even wiser students, Rabbi Elazar Hisma and Rabbi Yohanan ben Gudgeda, who had neither bread nor clothing, and resolved to seat them at the head of the academy. When they came only at his second summons, he told them he was granting them not authority but servitude.
horayot-10a-18-20.why: The Gemara has read the verse about King Azariah living in an "independent house" to mean that until then a king is a servant of the people; Rabban Gamliel's words to his appointees illustrate that office is servitude.

people.name: Rabban Gamliel
people.about: Leader of the academy, traveling on the ship, who appoints the two students.

people.name: Rabbi Yehoshua
people.about: His fellow traveler, who brought extra flour and points out the two poor students.

people.name: Rabbi Elazar Ḥisma
people.about: A student said to be able to calculate the drops in the sea, yet without bread or clothing.

people.name: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda
people.about: The second such student, appointed together with Rabbi Elazar Ḥisma.

terms.meaning: To give them a leading position in the academy, the house of study.

horayot-12b-1-1.note: Rabbi Yosei tells of Yosef ben Eilim of Tzippori, a priest appointed to replace a High Priest who had become temporarily disqualified. Once the disqualification passed and the original High Priest returned, the other priests would not let Yosef ben Eilim serve at all, neither as High Priest nor as an ordinary priest. The Gemara explains: not as High Priest because two equal High Priests would breed enmity, and not as an ordinary priest because one may raise a person in holiness but not lower him.
horayot-12b-1-1.why: The discussion asks what happens to a stand-in High Priest after the original returns; Rabbi Meir says he keeps the High Priest's duties, and Rabbi Yosei cites this incident for his view that the stand-in may serve in neither role.

people.name: Rabbi Yosei
people.about: The Sage who reports the incident.

people.name: Yosef ben Eilim
people.about: A priest from Tzippori appointed as substitute High Priest, then barred from serving.

terms.meaning: The chief priest of the Temple in Jerusalem, who alone performed certain rites, such as those of Yom Kippur.
Any priest descended from Aaron who served in the Temple without the High Priest's special rank.

horayot-13b-10-17.note: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, the Nasi, saw the academy rise for Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Natan just as for him, and while they were away he set new rules marking his higher rank. Offended, they plotted to unseat him by asking him to teach tractate Uktzin, which he did not know, but Rabbi Ya'akov ben Korshei overheard and recited it aloud behind his room until he learned it; he passed the test and had the two expelled. Readmitted after they kept tossing in notes with questions and answers, they were penalized by having their teachings cited only as "Others" and "Some say." Years later Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's son questioned this, and his father then taught a ruling "in the name of Rabbi Meir."
horayot-13b-10-17.why: The Gemara has quoted a teaching on how the academy shows honor to the Nasi, the Hakham and the deputy Nasi; Rabbi Yohanan says it was taught in Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's day, and this story tells how those rules came about.

people.name: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
people.about: The Nasi, head of the Sages, who sets the rules of honor and has his rivals expelled.

people.name: Rabbi Meir
people.about: The Hakham of the academy, who plots with Rabbi Natan to unseat the Nasi.

people.name: Rabbi Natan
people.about: The deputy Nasi, whose father, the text says, was the Babylonian Exilarch; he later goes to make peace.

people.name: Rabbi Ya'akov ben Korshei
people.about: A Sage who overhears the plot and quietly helps the Nasi prepare.

people.name: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi
people.about: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's son and successor, who teaches the story's aftermath to his own son.

terms.meaning: The president of the Sages' court and academy, the highest office among the Sages.
Literally "sage"; here a named office in the academy, ranking below the Nasi.
Head of the court, second to the Nasi.
A tractate of the Mishna on the ritual impurity of stalks and peels of produce, known as obscure.

horayot-14a-3-3.note: Rav Yosef was known as "Sinai," a master of vast knowledge, and Rabba as "one who uproots mountains," a sharp reasoner. The Babylonian Sages sent to the Land of Israel asking which should take precedence, and the answer came back that Sinai is preferable, since everyone needs the owner of the wheat. Even so, Rav Yosef declined the post; Rabba led the yeshiva for twenty-two years before Rav Yosef took over, and all that time Rav Yosef would not even have a bloodletter come to his home.
horayot-14a-3-3.why: Rabbi Yohanan has just reported a dispute between Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and the Rabbis over whether the learned scholar or the incisive one is preferable; the Gemara shows the question deciding a real appointment.

people.name: Rav Yosef
people.about: Called "Sinai" for his knowledge; chosen for the post but declined it in deference to Rabba.

people.name: Rabba
people.about: Called "one who uproots mountains" for his sharp reasoning; headed the yeshiva for twenty-two years.

terms.meaning: An academy of Torah study; its head was the leading Sage of the place.
A picture for the scholar who holds the raw material of the tradition, the sources everyone else depends on.
A healer who drew blood, a common treatment at the time; summoning one home was a sign of status.

horayot-14a-4-4.note: Abaye, Rava, Rabbi Zeira and Rabba bar Mattana were studying together and needed someone to head their group. They agreed that whoever made a statement that could not be refuted would lead. Every statement was refuted except Abaye's, and when Rabba saw Abaye lift his head, he said to him: Nahmani, begin and speak.
horayot-14a-4-4.why: The discussion is about which kind of scholar should lead, the learned one or the incisive one; this group settles its leader by a test of sharp argument, and the Gemara goes on to ask which of two of its members is preferable.

people.name: Abaye
people.about: The one member of the group whose statement was not refuted; Rabba calls him by his name, Nahmani.

people.name: Rava
people.about: A member of the study group.

people.name: Rabbi Zeira
people.about: A member of the study group.

people.name: Rabba bar Mattana
people.about: A member of the study group.

people.name: Rabba
people.about: The Sage who sees Abaye lift his head and invites him to begin.
